thread:
santiago: Hey team — after upgrading my app dependency to the newest Redwood SDK I get an import error on startup, app won't boot. Error below, happening in a clean venv on Python 3.11:

```
> File "/opt/app/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/__init__.py", line 12, in <module>
>     from redwood.client import RedwoodClient
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood.client'
```

I ran `pip install redwood --upgrade` and `python -c 'import redwood; print(redwood.__file__)'` — it points to something odd. Any quick checks I should do? I'm blocked for a deploy.

support-bot: Thanks @santiago — ticket #SUP-8231 created and assigned to emma.

emma: thanks for the quick repro. Can you paste `pip show redwood` and `pip freeze | grep redwood` and your `python --version`? Also did you install via pip or poetry?

santiago: pip output below:
```
$ python --version
Python 3.11.4
$ pip show redwood
Name: redwood
Version: 0.1.1
Summary: A tiny package for plotting redwood trees
Home-page: https://example.org/redwood
Location: /opt/app/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages
Requires:
Required-by:
$ pip freeze | grep redwood || true
redwood==0.1.1
```

santiago: I also have `pyproject.toml` which lists `redwood-inference = "^1.5.0"` — weird that pip show shows `redwood`. I mostly used `pip` (not poetry) to install in the Dockerfile.

emma: ah — this looks like a PyPI name collision. There's a different package named `redwood` on PyPI that is unrelated. Our official client is published as `redwood-inference` (and we also publish a `redwood-sdk` alias). When you `pip install redwood` you get the wrong package.

emma: Quick fix steps — run these in your build/container:
```
pip uninstall -y redwood
pip install --no-cache-dir redwood-inference==1.5.2
python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__version__, redwood.__file__)"
```
That should show `1.5.2` and point to site-packages/redwood_inference (or redwood package installed by our wheel). If you use poetry, change the dep to `redwood-inference` in pyproject and `poetry lock && poetry install`.

josh: Confirming — we've seen this a few times. On older Dockerfiles people ran `pip install -r requirements.txt` where a stray `redwood` ended up in the constraints, or scripts run `pip install redwood` from a quick backfill. We're planning two follow-ups: (1) update our README & quickstart to emphasize `pip install redwood-inference` and (2) publish a small advisory script `redwood-cli` that warns if the installed package metadata doesn't match our expected author/summary.

josh: For the short-term, if anyone hits similar in CI you can add a verification step to your Dockerfile:
```
python -c "import pkgutil, importlib.metadata as m; print(m.metadata('redwood-inference').get('Name'))"
```
or simply fail fast when `getattr(redwood, '__version__', None)` is None or unexpected.

santiago: Ran the uninstall/install steps — confirmed fixed. After reinstall:
```
$ python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__version__, redwood.__file__)"
1.5.2 /opt/app/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood_inference/__init__.py
```

santiago: Deploy resumed, thanks! :raised_hands:

emma: great — marking support ticket resolved. josh — can you add the advisory to the SDK repo and maybe a CI check for our sample Dockerfiles?

josh: yup I'll open a small PR today adding the README note + a pre-flight check script. Thanks for the report @santiago.

santiago: thanks all.
